identity.name: Mongolian People's Republic
native_names: Бүгд Найрамдах Монгол Ард Улс (Bügd Nairamdakh Mongol Ard Uls)

land.text: the whole of Outer Mongolia: the constitution 'adopted by the first Great Khural in November 1924, proclaimed the Mongolian People's Republic' (infobox: Predecessor Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Great Mongol State row runs to 1925 and this row starts in 1926; 1924-1925 is covered by this dossier's new keyframe.

land.text: the whole country: the 1992 constitution 'entering into force in February' created the State of Mongolia

successors.note: Cliopatria's Mongolia row begins in 1992; the republic ended on 12 February 1992 (infobox).

capitals.name: Ulaanbaatar
capitals.note: Infobox capital Ulaanbaatar (no coordinates on the page; lon/lat from the gazetteer). Urga before 1924 (see great-mongol-state).

correction.text: the Great Mongol State's 1924 outline, held by the republic from 26 November 1924

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Great Mongol State shape carries 1924-1925 and this row begins in 1926, but the republic was proclaimed on 26 November 1924 (infobox 'Established: 26 November 1924'), so 1924-1925 is drawn here with the same outline. The page's 1,564,116 km2 (no year) is within 0.4% of the shape.
1,569,574 km2 against the infobox 1,564,116 km2 (no year given; ratio 1.003). The page records no territorial change in 1924-1926.
One cell (253 km2) at 105.04E 41.65N differs from 1926: digitisation noise on the Gobi frontier; no page dates a border change.
The 1927 cell at 105.04E 41.65N is dropped again; noise.
Two cells added on the southern frontier (97.3-105.0E 41.7-42.7N) and three dropped (105.8-119.5E 42.0-47.3N), about 0.05% of the area; noise, no page dates a change.

Japan 'invaded Manchuria and set up the puppet state of Manchukuo' in 1931-1932 (page), which makes Manchukuo the eastern neighbour; the shape differs from 1929 by 3 cells (about 0.05%): noise. No page moves the frontier.

1,569,171 km2; two southern cells dropped (97.3-105.8E 42.0-42.7N). The 1939 Khalkhin Gol fighting left the line unchanged: infobox 'Status quo ante bellum; enforcement of border claims in accordance with the Soviet and Mongolian interpretation' (Mongolia's line about 16 km east of the river, just east of Nomonhan, which the shape already contains).

Two cells at 87.9-88.2E 49.2-49.4N (the Altai corner) appear in 1940-1942 and vanish in 1943: noise. The 1941 Soviet-Japanese agreements 'respecting the borders of Mongolia and Manchukuo' (Khalkhin Gol page) moved no land.
Same outline as the 1940-1942 shape without the Altai-corner cells.

One cell (253 km2) at 90.82E 45.9N is added, the Baitag Bogd direction, and kept in 1945-1949. The referendum page reports an independence vote on 20 October 1945 and no boundary terms: 'The page doesn't define the extent of Outer Mongolia's territory'.

unverified (page silent): 1,572,665 km2, the one outlier; seven cells (about 1,770 km2) at 109.8-116.2E 42.5-45.8N appear only in 1946 (absent in 1945 and 1947), on the Inner Mongolian frontier toward Dolon Nur, which the Soviet-Mongolian group took in August 1945 and the Red Army was to leave by 3 May 1946. No page opened says Mongolia held or annexed that land, so it is treated as a short occupation or an artefact (0.2% of the area); a gap-filler may drop the cells.

1,569,937 km2. The Baitag Bogd fighting of 5 June-July 1947 ended with 'the lands occupied by the Mongols were returned' to China in early July, so the outline is Mongolia's own; the cell at 90.82E 45.9N stays in 1947-1949.
Identical to the 1945 shape (0 cell difference).

1,569,528 km2, held to 1990: 'the border has remained where it is' since the 1960s. The 1950 shape drops the 90.82E 45.9N cell and one other and adds one at 105.04E 41.65N (noise). The treaty of 26 December 1962 delimited the frontier, demarcation ran 1963-1964 and 'a final treaty with a detailed set of maps' was agreed on 30 June 1964; the page reports no exchange of land and gives no shares for the Baitag Bogd area.
Same outline as 1950-1990; the state ends on 12 February 1992.
New keyframe for the last weeks: Cliopatria gives the 1992 year to its Mongolia row, but the republic lasted to 12 February 1992 (infobox 'Dissolution: 12 February 1992'). Same outline as 1991.

ledger.note: 26 November 1924: the Mongolian People's Republic is proclaimed. 'adopted by the first Great Khural in November 1924, proclaimed the Mongolian People's Republic' (infobox Established 26 November 1924; Predecessor Bogd Khanate of Mongolia; area 1,564,116 km2).

region.text: the strip between the Khalkhin Gol and the line 16 km east, just east of Nomonhan

ledger.note: May 1939: fighting on the Khalkhin Gol begins. 'The battles began on 11 May 1939.' The Japanese 'maintained that the border between Manchukuo and Mongolia was the Khalkhin Gol', while the Mongolian and Soviet side held that it 'ran 16 kilometres east of the river, just east of Nomonhan'. The page's coordinates for the battle area are 47.73N 118.59E.

16 September 1939: ceasefire on the Khalkhin Gol. 'The Soviet Union and Japan agreed to a cease-fire on 15 September; it took effect the following day'; result 'Status quo ante bellum; enforcement of border claims in accordance with the Soviet and Mongolian interpretation' (no change to the shape).

region.text: Dolon Nur and Kalgan in Mengjiang, the Japanese puppet state in Inner Mongolia

ledger.note: August 1945: Mongolian cavalry enter Inner Mongolia with the Red Army. The invasion began 8 August; 'the Soviet-Mongolian Cavalry-Mechanized Group entered Inner Mongolia and quickly took Dolon Nur and Kalgan' (the page gives no date for the advance; Mongolia 16,000 troops, 72 killed). The page does not say Mongolia kept any land.

2 September 1945: the fighting ends. 'The Kwantung Army officially surrendered on 16 August, although fighting continued until 2 September, when the Japanese Instrument of Surrender was signed.' The Red Army was to withdraw by 3 May 1946, handing much of Inner Mongolia to Communist-held territories.

region.text: the Baitag Bogd (Peitashan, Beitashan) mountain area on the Mongolia-Xinjiang frontier

ledger.note: 5 June 1947: Mongolian troops attack at Baitag Bogd. 'on June 5, 1947, the Mongolian border guards suddenly attacked the Ma Xinzhen area'; on 15 June Mongolia's foreign ministry declared 'The Baitag-Bogd mountains are not Chinese, but the territory of the Mongolian People's Republic'. The page puts the mountains in Xinjiang and says China held the southern part.

Early July 1947: the Mongols give the land back. 'in early July 1947, the lands occupied by the Mongols were returned' to China. The frontier there was divided only in 1962 ('when Mongolia and China demarcated and established a border', shares not stated).

region.text: the whole country passes to the State of Mongolia

ledger.note: 12 February 1992: the people's republic ends. Infobox 'Ended: 12 February 1992' (communist state abolished; the constitution adopted in January 1992 'entering into force in February'); the state continues as Mongolia.

wars.name: Battles of Khalkhin Gol

zones.text: the Khalkhin Gol strip east of the river

wars.outcome: Soviet-Mongolian victory; ceasefire agreed 15 September (effective 16 September 1939); 'Status quo ante bellum; enforcement of border claims in accordance with the Soviet and Mongolian interpretation'.
wars.note: Fighting began 11 May 1939; Japan encircled and destroyed in August (MPR page). The Soviet-Japanese agreements of 1941 'respecting the borders of Mongolia and Manchukuo' are not described.

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria (Mongolian cavalry in Inner Mongolia)
wars.outcome: The Soviet-Mongolian Cavalry-Mechanized Group took Dolon Nur and Kalgan from Mengjiang; fighting ended 2 September 1945; the Red Army withdrew by 3 May 1946. The page does not say Mongolia kept territory.
wars.note: Mongolia is listed among the belligerents (16,000 troops); the MPR page says only that the Soviets 'used Mongolia as one base'.

wars.name: Battle of Baitag Bogd (Beitashan incident)
belligerents: Ospan Batur's Kazakh and Dungan raiders
wars.outcome: Infobox result 'Status quo ante bellum'; the lands the Mongols had occupied were returned to China in early July 1947; the frontier was divided in the 1962 demarcation.
wars.note: Raids June 1946-July 1947, Mongolian attack 5 June 1947, Soviet aircraft involved (TASS denied it). The infobox span is 1946-1948.

certainty.note: The frontier with China was undemarcated and disputed (Baitag Bogd 1947, the Khalkhin Gol line 1939); the Soviet frontier follows older treaty lines that were not opened, so it is treated as the era's level.

The China-Mongolia frontier was delimited by the treaty of 26 December 1962, demarcated 1963-1964 and fixed by a final treaty with maps on 30 June 1964; 'the border has remained where it is'. The Soviet frontier was not checked on any page.

notes: Cliopatria's 14 shapes are one outline (modern Mongolia, 1.569 M km2 against the infobox 1.564 M km2) with 1-3 cell edge differences; only 1946 differs by 7 cells. No page opened dates a frontier change after 1924 except the unresolved Baitag Bogd and Khalkhin Gol disputes. Recognition: the Republic of China treated Outer Mongolia as Chinese until the Sino-Soviet treaty of 14 August 1945, the referendum of 20 October 1945 and recognition in January 1946 (referendum page); the 1924 Sino-Soviet treaty still counted Mongolia as Chinese (Revolution of 1921 page). The ea-08 dossier for the Republic of China may want a nominal-claim note; no ledger event type fits. The Soviet Union's client relation (treaty 1921, verbal mutual aid 1934, formal agreement 1936, 650,000 Soviet troops in 1945, secret annex of 1966, withdrawal 1987-1992) belongs in the union-of-soviet-socialist-republics dossier (eu-17) as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart mongolian-people-s-republic; the pages give no start date for stationed troops. Not settled: the Baitag Bogd shares of 1962 (page silent), the 1946 outlier cells, the date and terms of the 1941 Soviet-Japanese frontier agreements, the Tuvan People's Republic frontier (annexed by the Soviet Union in 1944; no Mongolian-Tuvan frontier date on any page opened), and the Soviet frontier. No ruler list: the page gives heads of state and party leaders in overlapping tables (Choibalsan 1928-1952, Tsedenbal 1952-1984, Batmonkh 1984-1990), not a clean strip. Counterparts needing dossiers: Manchukuo and Mengjiang (Japanese puppet states, not Cliopatria rows). Gazetteer names used but missing: Baitag Bogd, Dolon Nur.
